source: Directive tables of the Bareos 25.1.2 Director as carried by odir (crates/odir/src/commands/show_items.rs) plus Onesimus extensions (crates/odir/src/config_check.rs EXTENSIONS)
description: A Storage resource tells the Director how to reach a Storage Daemon and which of its devices and media type to use.

examples.title: Disk storage
examples.config:
Storage {
  Name = File
  Address = backup.example.com
  Password = "storage-secret"
  Device = FileStorage
  Media Type = File
  Maximum Concurrent Jobs = 10
}

directives.name: Name
directives.description: Name of the Storage resource as jobs and pools refer to it.

examples.console: configure add storage name=File address=backup.example.com password=storage-secret device=FileStorage mediatype=File

directives.name: Description
directives.description: Free text describing the storage.

examples.console: configure add storage name=File address=backup.example.com password=storage-secret device=FileStorage mediatype=File description="Disk storage in the server room"

directives.name: Protocol
directives.description: Protocol to the storage: Native, or NDMP for NDMP tape servers.

examples.console: configure add storage name=File address=backup.example.com password=storage-secret device=FileStorage mediatype=File protocol=Native

directives.name: Auth Type
directives.description: Authentication for NDMP storage: None, Clear or MD5.

examples.console: configure add storage name=File address=backup.example.com password=storage-secret device=FileStorage mediatype=File authtype=None

directives.name: Address
directives.description: Host name or IP address of the Storage Daemon, as the File Daemons must reach it: the Director passes it on to the client. Do not use localhost when clients run on other hosts.

examples.console: configure add storage name=File password=storage-secret device=FileStorage mediatype=File address=backup.example.com

directives.name: Lan Address
directives.description: Address used instead of Address for clients in passive mode on a separate LAN.

examples.console: configure add storage name=File address=backup.example.com password=storage-secret device=FileStorage mediatype=File lanaddress=10.0.0.5

directives.name: Port
directives.description: TCP port of the Storage Daemon.

examples.console: configure add storage name=File address=backup.example.com password=storage-secret device=FileStorage mediatype=File port=9103

directives.name: Username
directives.description: User name for NDMP authentication.

examples.console: configure add storage name=File address=backup.example.com password=storage-secret device=FileStorage mediatype=File username=ndmp

directives.name: Password
directives.description: Password shared with the Storage Daemon's Director resource (and TLS-PSK key).

examples.console: configure add storage name=File address=backup.example.com device=FileStorage mediatype=File password=storage-secret

directives.name: Device
directives.description: Name of a Device (or Autochanger) resource in the Storage Daemon. It must match the name there exactly. Several devices may be listed.

examples.console: configure add storage name=File address=backup.example.com password=storage-secret mediatype=File device=FileStorage

directives.name: Media Type
directives.description: Media type of the volumes this storage writes. The Director only uses volumes of this media type with it, so different kinds of media (or different directories of file storage) need different media types. It must match Media Type of the device in the Storage Daemon.

examples.console: configure add storage name=File address=backup.example.com password=storage-secret device=FileStorage mediatype=File

directives.name: Auto Changer
directives.description: The device is an autochanger (tape library); slots and barcodes are used for label, update slots and mount.

examples.console: configure add storage name=File address=backup.example.com password=storage-secret device=FileStorage mediatype=File autochanger=yes

directives.name: Enabled
directives.description: A disabled storage is not used for new jobs; enable/disable storage change it at run time.

examples.console: configure add storage name=File address=backup.example.com password=storage-secret device=FileStorage mediatype=File enabled=yes

directives.name: Allow Compression
directives.description: Allow software compression by the File Daemon for jobs writing here. Set it to no for tape drives that compress in hardware.

examples.console: configure add storage name=File address=backup.example.com password=storage-secret device=FileStorage mediatype=File allowcompression=yes

directives.name: Heartbeat Interval
directives.description: Interval of keep-alive packets to the Storage Daemon. 0 switches it off. Times are written as a number with a unit: seconds, minutes, hours, days, weeks, months, quarters or years (abbreviations such as 30d, 12h or 1y work too); several parts add up ("1 month 15 days"), and a plain number means seconds.

examples.console: configure add storage name=File address=backup.example.com password=storage-secret device=FileStorage mediatype=File heartbeatinterval=60

directives.name: Cache Status Interval
directives.description: How long the Director caches the status of the Storage Daemon. Times are written as a number with a unit: seconds, minutes, hours, days, weeks, months, quarters or years (abbreviations such as 30d, 12h or 1y work too); several parts add up ("1 month 15 days"), and a plain number means seconds.

examples.console: configure add storage name=File address=backup.example.com password=storage-secret device=FileStorage mediatype=File cachestatusinterval=30

directives.name: Maximum Concurrent Jobs
directives.description: How many jobs may use this storage at the same time. With disk storage and several devices it can be raised; the device's own Maximum Concurrent Jobs in the Storage Daemon limits as well (the Director cannot read that one).

examples.console: configure add storage name=File address=backup.example.com password=storage-secret device=FileStorage mediatype=File maximumconcurrentjobs=10

directives.name: Maximum Concurrent Read Jobs
directives.description: How many of the concurrent jobs may read (restore, copy, migrate source); 0 means no own limit.

examples.console: configure add storage name=File address=backup.example.com password=storage-secret device=FileStorage mediatype=File maximumconcurrentreadjobs=2

directives.name: Paired Storage
directives.description: For NDMP: the native storage that holds the data of an NDMP backup that Bareos stores itself.

examples.console: configure add storage name=File address=backup.example.com password=storage-secret device=FileStorage mediatype=File pairedstorage=File

directives.name: Maximum Bandwidth Per Job
directives.description: Limits the bandwidth of each job on this storage. Speeds take the suffixes k/s, m/s (powers of 1024) or kb/s, mb/s (powers of 1000); a plain number means bytes per second.

examples.console: configure add storage name=File address=backup.example.com password=storage-secret device=FileStorage mediatype=File maximumbandwidthperjob="50 m/s"

directives.name: Collect Statistics
directives.description: Deprecated: collect device statistics in the catalog.

directives.name: NDMP Changer Device
directives.description: Changer device of an NDMP tape server.

examples.console: configure add storage name=File address=backup.example.com password=storage-secret device=FileStorage mediatype=File ndmpchangerdevice=/dev/sg0

directives.name: TLS Authenticate
directives.description: Use TLS only to authenticate the peer and switch back to an unencrypted connection afterwards. The data then travels in clear text, so this is meant for networks that are protected otherwise. Bareos' default TLS-PSK setup does not need it.

examples.console: configure add storage name=File address=backup.example.com password=storage-secret device=FileStorage mediatype=File tlsauthenticate=no

directives.name: TLS Enable
directives.description: Enable TLS for this connection. Since Bareos 18.2 TLS is on by default and uses TLS-PSK with the password of the resource, so no certificates are needed; set it to no only for peers that cannot speak TLS.

examples.console: configure add storage name=File address=backup.example.com password=storage-secret device=FileStorage mediatype=File tlsenable=yes

directives.name: TLS Require
directives.description: Refuse connections that do not use TLS. With the default (yes) a peer without TLS cannot connect; set it to no only during a migration from very old clients.

examples.console: configure add storage name=File address=backup.example.com password=storage-secret device=FileStorage mediatype=File tlsrequire=yes

directives.name: TLS Cipher List
directives.description: OpenSSL cipher list for TLS 1.2 and older, colon separated. Leave it empty to use the OpenSSL defaults; restrict it only when a security policy demands specific ciphers.

examples.console: configure add storage name=File address=backup.example.com password=storage-secret device=FileStorage mediatype=File tlscipherlist=PSK-AES256-GCM-SHA384:PSK-AES128-GCM-SHA256

directives.name: TLS Cipher Suites
directives.description: OpenSSL cipher suites for TLS 1.3, colon separated. Empty means the OpenSSL defaults.

examples.console: configure add storage name=File address=backup.example.com password=storage-secret device=FileStorage mediatype=File tlsciphersuites=TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384:TLS_CHACHA20_POLY1305_SHA256

directives.name: TLS DH File
directives.description: PEM file with Diffie-Hellman parameters for the DH key exchange of TLS 1.2. Without it, ephemeral DH ciphers are not offered; ECDHE and PSK ciphers do not need it.

examples.console: configure add storage name=File address=backup.example.com password=storage-secret device=FileStorage mediatype=File tlsdhfile=/etc/bareos/tls/dh2048.pem

directives.name: TLS Protocol
directives.description: Restricts the TLS protocol versions in OpenSSL syntax, for example to forbid old versions. Empty means the OpenSSL default.

examples.console: configure add storage name=File address=backup.example.com password=storage-secret device=FileStorage mediatype=File tlsprotocol="-ALL, +TLSv1.2, +TLSv1.3"

directives.name: TLS Verify Peer
directives.description: With certificate based TLS: check the peer's certificate against the CA and, for a server, against TLS Allowed CN. It has no effect with TLS-PSK.

examples.console: configure add storage name=File address=backup.example.com password=storage-secret device=FileStorage mediatype=File tlsverifypeer=yes

directives.name: TLS Ca Certificate File
directives.description: PEM file with the CA certificates used to verify the peer's certificate. Needed for certificate based TLS when TLS Verify Peer is on (or use TLS CA Certificate Dir).

examples.console: configure add storage name=File address=backup.example.com password=storage-secret device=FileStorage mediatype=File tlscacertificatefile=/etc/bareos/tls/ca.pem

directives.name: TLS Ca Certificate Dir
directives.description: Directory of hashed CA certificates (as made by openssl rehash), an alternative to TLS CA Certificate File.

examples.console: configure add storage name=File address=backup.example.com password=storage-secret device=FileStorage mediatype=File tlscacertificatedir=/etc/ssl/certs

directives.name: TLS Certificate Revocation List
directives.description: PEM file with a certificate revocation list; certificates on it are refused.

examples.console: configure add storage name=File address=backup.example.com password=storage-secret device=FileStorage mediatype=File tlscertificaterevocationlist=/etc/bareos/tls/crl.pem

directives.name: TLS Certificate
directives.description: PEM file with the own certificate for certificate based TLS. Goes together with TLS Key.

examples.console: configure add storage name=File address=backup.example.com password=storage-secret device=FileStorage mediatype=File tlscertificate=/etc/bareos/tls/bareos-dir.pem

directives.name: TLS Key
directives.description: PEM file with the private key of TLS Certificate. Keep it readable for the daemon user only.

examples.console: configure add storage name=File address=backup.example.com password=storage-secret device=FileStorage mediatype=File tlskey=/etc/bareos/tls/bareos-dir.key

directives.name: TLS Allowed CN
directives.description: Common names a peer certificate may carry; others are refused when TLS Verify Peer is on. Repeat the directive for several names.

examples.console: configure add storage name=File address=backup.example.com password=storage-secret device=FileStorage mediatype=File tlsallowedcn=client1.example.com
